page_01: A lion's roar can be heard up to 5 miles away!
page_02: Elephants flap their big ears to cool down on hot days.
page_03: Giraffes are the tallest animals on Earth.
page_04: Every zebra has its own stripe pattern, just like a fingerprint.
page_05: Hippos can hold their breath underwater for about 5 minutes.
page_06: Cheetahs are the fastest runners on land, as fast as a car on a highway!
page_07: A rhino's horn is made of keratin, just like your fingernails.
page_08: Meerkats take turns standing guard while their family looks for food.
page_09: Ostriches lay the biggest eggs of any bird alive today.
page_10: Warthogs kneel on their front knees to nibble short grass.
page_11: Flamingos get their pink color from the food they eat.
page_12: Gorillas build a fresh leafy bed to sleep in every night.
page_13: Ring-tailed lemurs hold their tails up high so their group can follow.
page_14: A chameleon's tongue can be longer than its whole body!
page_15: Sloths move so slowly that tiny algae can grow on their fur!
page_16: A toucan's giant beak is light because it is full of tiny air pockets.
page_17: Jaguars love water and are very strong swimmers.
page_18: Tree frogs flash their big eyes to surprise hungry animals.
page_19: Macaws use their strong, curved beaks like an extra hand for climbing.
page_20: Capybaras are the biggest rodents in the world.
page_21: Llamas hum to talk to each other.
page_22: Giant pandas spend about 12 hours a day eating bamboo.
page_23: Red pandas spend most of their lives up in the trees.
page_24: A tiger's stripes are on its skin as well as its fur.
page_25: Orangutans use big leaves as umbrellas when it rains.
page_26: Snow leopards can't roar, but they can purr like a house cat.
page_27: Yaks have long, shaggy coats that keep them warm high in the mountains.
page_28: Komodo dragons are the biggest lizards in the world.
page_29: Only male peafowl, called peacocks, grow the giant fan of tail feathers.
page_30: Grizzly bears catch salmon as the fish leap up waterfalls.
page_31: Only male moose grow antlers, and they grow a new set every year.
page_32: A beaver's front teeth never stop growing.
page_33: Wolves live and hunt together in family groups called packs.
page_34: Bald eagles build some of the biggest bird nests in the world.
page_35: Raccoons have very sensitive front paws that work almost like hands.
page_36: Owls fly almost silently thanks to their soft, fluffy feathers.
page_37: Bison can run up to 35 miles per hour.
page_38: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards.
page_39: Prairie dogs greet each other with a kiss.
page_40: A camel's hump stores fat, not water.
page_41: Fennec foxes have giant ears that help them stay cool in the desert.
page_42: Some armadillos can roll up into a tight ball.
page_43: Desert tortoises dig burrows to hide from the hot sun.
page_44: Roadrunners can run about 20 miles per hour.
page_45: Alligators can have about 80 teeth at a time.
page_46: River otters love to slide down muddy banks just for fun.
page_47: Polar bears have tiny bumps on their paws that help them grip the ice.
page_48: Emperor penguins can dive deeper than any other bird.
page_49: A newborn kangaroo is about the size of a jellybean.
page_50: A koala's fingerprints look almost exactly like a human's.
